newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish exporters say exports fell in September.
newsitem.headline: Turkish exporters say exports fell in September.

text.p: Turkey's biggest exporters' body said on Friday total September exports were $1.94 billion, down three percent from the same 1995 month.
The influential Turkish Exporters Assembly (TIM) estimated in a statement January-September exports in 1996 at $16.74 billion, up four percent from the same period last year.
Official figures were not yet available.
"If appropriate measures are not taken to stop the fall in exports, Turkey will be facing serious problems," TIM chairman Okan Oguz said in the statement.
TIM said ready-to-wear exports, Turkey's top money spinner, fell by 26 percent in September to $496.43 million from $670.87 million in the same month last year.

Olive and olive oil exports plunged 46 percent to $5.2 million in September compared to the same 1995 month. Hazelnut exports fell 40 percent to $63.19 million and leather exports dropped 19 percent to $60.6 million, it said.
But tobacco exports rose 190 percent to $45.0 million in September and cement exports gained 129 percent to $54.96 million.
Official figures announced on Wednesday put Turkey's trade deficit in February at $1.13 billion, up sharply from $732 million in February 1995.
Official trade data has been delayed by what officials call technical difficulties arising from Turkey's customs union with the European Union since January 1, 1996.
